claims: TPS is a U.S. immigration benefit granted to foreign nationals who cannot return safely to their home country due to ongoing armed conflict, environmental disasters, or extraordinary, temporary conditions.
TPS eligibility requires being a national of a designated country.
TPS eligibility requires having filed during a specific registration period.
TPS eligibility requires having been continuously present in the U.S. since a specified date.
TPS recipients receive an Employment Authorization Document (EAD).
TPS provides protection from detention or removal.
TPS is granted for 6 to 18-month periods.
TPS may be extended by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
TPS does not provide a direct path to lawful permanent resident status (green card).
TPS does not provide a direct path to citizenship.
As of 2025-2026, TPS designated countries include Afghanistan, Haiti, Venezuela, El Salvador, Honduras, Ukraine, and others.
TPS is administered by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
TPS was established by the Immigration Act of 1990.
